title: A Garden for the Oath Again
premise: Oscar Whitlock was born in Hollowmere, the last valley where magic cannot follow, and raised by a guild of oath-keepers who have forgotten what their oaths once bound. When the old gods stir beneath the mountain and begin answering prayers again, Oscar learns her grandmother sold her own soul to the court below to seal the valley's peace—and that the debt now passes to Oscar as heir. To save her grandmother from dissolution, Oscar must leave the only home she's known, infiltrate the subterranean court wearing a stolen identity, and win back the soul before the equinox. She succeeds, but at the cost of her guild name: she returns not as an invisible Whitlock but as the woman who bargained with gods—and loved one of them.
about_author: Hazel Yarrow is the pen name of a former botanist who spent a decade cataloguing alpine wildflowers before turning to fiction about stubborn women and patient landscapes. She writes fantasy rooted in folklore, debt, and the quiet violence of inheritance.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In Hollowmere, where spells die at the tree line, Oscar tends the guild's neglected garden and performs hollow rituals for a dying order. Her grandmother, Maren, begins speaking to people who aren't there. The emotional beat is quiet dread—the first crack in a life built on staying small.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A neighbor's prayer is answered impossibly; crops bloom out of season. Maren confesses fragments: a bargain made beneath the mountain, a soul held as surety. Oscar realizes the gods' return isn't grace—it's collection. Beat: terror braided with a strange, unwelcome thrill of purpose.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with a flashback chapter from Maren. Searching the guild archive, Oscar finds the original oath: protection purchased with a soul, renewed each generation. Maren's memory-chapters reveal her youth, her love for a god, and the price she paid. Beat: grief reframing love as both wound and inheritance.

chapters.title: Leaving the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. On the eve of the equinox deadline, Oscar crosses the boundary where magic resumes—painfully, like learning to breathe again. She carries Maren's old tokens and a map stitched into a garden apron. Beat: vertigo and exhilaration; the world is larger and crueler than promised.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Traveling toward the mountain, Oscar trades favors with hedge-witches and river-spirits, learning the rules of a world that prices everything. She meets Wren, a charming courier who owes the court himself. Beat: wary alliance; Oscar practices being someone new and finds she likes her.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Descending through root-tunnels into the god-court, Oscar poses as a debt-broker's clerk. She witnesses how souls are kept: potted, pruned, blooming in rows—a terrible mirror of her garden. Beat: horror sharpened by recognition; she understands this place because it understands her.

chapters.title: The Gardener of Souls
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar locates Maren's soul among the pots and meets Vesper, the court's gardener-god—Maren's old love, now her keeper. He offers a trade: Maren's freedom for Oscar's service. Beat: temptation; duty and desire tangle until Oscar can't tell which she's resisting.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Alternating Oscar and Wren POVs. Oscar negotiates while Wren uncovers that the court itself is dying, sustained by hoarded souls. Oscar proposes instead to replant the souls in living soil above—restoring the gods by releasing them. Beat: audacity; the climax pivots on redefining what an oath can hold.

chapters.title: Equinox
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the equinox ceremony, Oscar swears a new oath before the assembled court: the valley will keep its gods alive willingly, gardens open to them, if every soul is freed. Vesper must choose between custody and trust. Beat: high-stakes climax; love offered as contract rather than sacrifice.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Oath Again
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, closing with Maren's. Home in Hollowmere, the guild becomes stewards of an open gate; Maren, restored and aging honestly, plants beside her granddaughter. Vesper visits at the tree line, neither crossing nor leaving. Beat: resolution—inheritance transformed from debt into cultivation, identity chosen rather than hidden.
